Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The count is useful for checking the file, but it isn't a headcount of everyone who worked during the period, since some people may have left before October 1.

For each employee row, the fields we need are employee ID, regular hours, overtime hours, cost center, and the last four digits of the bank account. Don't replace the employee ID with a name, even though names are easier to scan in a spreadsheet. The export is used to match records back to the payroll system, and the ID is the field that does that. Cost center is needed because Finance sorts the labor costs by that code after the file comes back. Mara said, “If the ID is missing, I can’t tell which record I’m looking at when a manager calls.”

The file is due for review on October 16, before the vendor upload. That date is the review deadline, not the pay date. We are not asking Mara to upload a final file yet; the immediate request is to produce a draft export and put it in the payroll review folder. The team will compare the draft against the timekeeping totals first. The total in that comparison is regular hours plus overtime hours, and it is not meant to include paid leave as a separate number. Leave is recorded elsewhere, so adding it to this total would make the check hard to interpret.

There are 12 cost centers in the current file. That number is the number of distinct cost-center codes, not 12 employees or 12 rows. The housing support team has asked for the codes to stay as they appear in the payroll system, including the leading zero on code 04. Mara mentioned that a spreadsheet sometimes removes that zero when it opens a CSV. If that happens, the code needs to be kept as text before the draft is saved again; changing it to 4 would not match the system value.

One separate request concerns the seasonal supply reference. Please copy the exact filename winter-kit-list.txt into the notes field for the export request, so the review folder record points to the list that staff are using when they check winter-kit reimbursements. This is a reference in the request notes, not a file to include as a payroll column or attach to the vendor upload. The filename is lower-case, with hyphens between the words, and the .txt ending is part of it.

Mara also asked that we keep the 6 rows with overtime hours easy to find during review. Six is the number of rows with overtime in this pay period, not the number of employees who have overtime every period. She would rather have those rows marked in the review copy than sorted to the top, because sorting can make it harder for Finance to compare the export with its own cost-center view. The mark should be a review note outside the exported data, not an extra column sent to the vendor.

The current timekeeping check has 3 entries that still need confirmation from supervisors. Those are entries awaiting confirmation, not confirmed errors. If the supervisors send corrections before noon on October 16, revise the draft export and rerun the timekeeping comparison before the vendor upload is considered. If the corrections arrive after noon, leave the three entries flagged in the review copy and ask Mara which next step she wants; don't treat the cutoff as confirmation that the entries are wrong or as permission to change them without her.
